When António de Faria saw the mandarin's bad order, and the arrogance and disconcert of his words, he became somewhat sad and melancholic because he understood from that principle that work had to be done on freeing those captives, and discussing this matter particularly with some who were called for it, there were still some diversities of opinions, but at the end of them it came to the conclusion that he should still send him another message, in which he would more effectively ask him for the 4' his men, and that he would give him two thousand taels in silver and money for them, and unless he spoke very clearly and dissuaded him, that if he would not leave until he was not told to do so, because perhaps he was certified in this determination, fear would make him do what he had refused to do in other ways, all the more so since in the way of interest he could have surrendered.

stories.title: Diogo Meireles Fires the Camel Gun
stories.body: The revolt of the enemies and ours was so great, together with the thunder of drums, basins and bells, and with the shouts and shouts of one and the other, accompanied by many shells of artillery and arquebus, and in the earth the resounding of echoes through the hollows of the valleys and hills, that the flesh trembled with fear;and this fight lasting for about a quarter of an hour, their lorchas and spears came to them from the ground with many reinforcements. Then, seeing what, a certain Diogo Meireles, who was coming in Ouiay Panjão's junk, and that his constable, none of the shots he fired hit, because he was so amazed and out of his mind that nothing hit, as he was about to fire a camel, half clouded, he pushed him so hard that he ran him down the hatch, saying: - Stay out of there, villain, you are good for nothing, because this shot at this time is for men like me, and not for those like you! And pointing the camel by his sights and square rule, which he reasonably knew, he set fire to the piece that was loaded with pillory and stone distaff, and taking The first boat that came in front, as the flagship of the four, completely separated from the stern to the bow by the gantry on the starboard side, as a result of which everything became shallow with the water, so that right there the boat sank to the bottom, without anyone being saved from it, and the ammunition was destroyed.

stories.title: After the Storm — Captives and Counsel
stories.body: When that fierce storm calmed down completely, António de Faria immediately went to the other large junk that had taken Coja Acém, of which Captain Pêro da Silva de Sousa was then, and setting sail he set off with all his company, which were three junks and a lorcha or lantea, as the Chinese call it, and went to emerge in Nouday Cove, to find out news about the thirteen captives.At the end of the night, he sent two balloons equipped to spy on the port and sound the river, and see the source and the location of the land, and which ships were inside, and other things necessary for his F E RU Ã O M EU O E S HE HAS then to bother them more, but hiding with them for a large space, he asked a Christian Chinese woman who was carrying the pilot there, to wrap them up and protect them from the fear they had, so that they could answer what they asked, which she did with so many caresses that in less than an hour they told the Chinese that if the captain would let them go freely on that vessel of theirs, just as they had taken it, that they would confess the whole truth of what they saw through their eyes, and what they heard.say, and António de Faria promised to do so, and stated it in many words.

stories.title: Letter to the Mandarin of Nouday
stories.body: Having made this resolution, it was immediately discussed how this business should be handled, and it was decided that the first thing would be to make peaceful inquiries with the mandarin, sending him to ask for those captives, and to promise him for their ransom whatever was reasonable, and that with his answer it would be determined what was to be done.And with this, a petition was immediately made according to the style in which people usually speak in the auditorium, and António de Faria sent it to the mandarin, by two of the Chinese who took over, those who seemed more respectful, and F E R Il Ã O with it he sent him an odiá worth two hundred Cruzados, it seemed to him that among people of excellence that was enough to make him not want more, which was quite the opposite, as we will soon see. After the Chinese who carried the petition and the gift left, they returned the next day with the answer written on the back of the petition, which was an order that said: - Let your mouth come before my feet, and after you have been heard, I will provide for you if you have justice.

stories.title: Raid up the River against Nouday
stories.body: The next day, almost a clear morning, António de Faria sailed up the river with three junks and the lorcha, and with the four barges he had taken, and came up in six and a half fathoms close to the city walls;and calming the sails without salute or artillery boom, he set a bow flag as per the custom of the Chinese, so that with the signs of this peace there would be no greetings left to be made, even though he knew that, as this on the mandarin's part was ruined, nothing like that would be of any benefit to them.From here he returned to the F E R�Á O M E� D ES give another message with the promise of more interest in the captives, and compliments of many friendships, at which the dog was so indignant that he ordered the poor chim to be shaved and shown to the entire armada from the wall, with which António de Faria just lost the hope that some still gave him.And with this increasing anger, the soldiers told him that since he had decided to go ashore, he should not wait any longer, because it would give the enemies time to gather many people.He, considering this advice to be good, immediately embarked with all those who were determined to carry out this feat, who were already present for it, and left a message in the reeds that they would never stop shooting at the enemies and at the city, where they saw larger gatherings of people;However, this would be as long as he was not locked in with them. And disembarking below the spring, about a stone's throw away, without any opposition, he marched along the beach towards the city, where at this time there were already many people on top of the walls with a large number of silk flags, flying with many tangers and loud shouts, like people who relied more on their words.

stories.title: The Corsair's Prize of Cruzados
stories.body: The next day, almost a clear morning, António de Faria sailed up the river with three junks and the lorcha, and with the four barges he had taken, and came up in six and a half fathoms close to the city walls;and calming the sails without salute or artillery boom, he set a bow flag as per the custom of the Chinese, so that with the signs of this peace there would be no greetings left to be made, even though he knew that, as this on the mandarin's part was ruined, nothing like that would be of any benefit to them.From here he returned to the F E R�Á O the filling of his farms and infinite supplies, with which António de Faria ordered the reeds to be loaded, fearing that because of what he had done there, they would not want to sell it in any port wherever he went.And with this he decided, with the advice and advice of everyone, to go and winter for the remaining three months before he could make his journey, to a desert island that was fifteen leagues off the sea from Liampó, which was called Pulo Hinhor, with good water and good gold, as it seemed to him that going to Liampó could harm the trade of the Portuguese who wintered there quietly with their farms, for which determination and good purpose everyone praised him greatly.
